title: Fire Protection Software: 5 Tools for Inspections and Leads
html:
Fire protection software starts with an inspection app that turns findings into proposals. Inspect Point is built for that job but does not publish a price, so you get a quote in a demo. Housecall Pro lists $59 a month for one user. Add a free Google Business Profile and a fast website so property managers can find you. Published prices below run from free to $299 a month.

Fire protection software has to do three jobs: record the inspection, turn deficiencies into paid work and bring in the next account. Most fire safety companies buy the first and neglect the other two. This guide sorts five tools by the job each one does, with the price each vendor publishes and one real limit for each.

Fire safety work is built on repeat inspections and follow-up repairs. A missed deficiency is a lost repair sale, and a missed inspection date is a lost account. So the tools below start with the inspection record, then the office work, then the marketing that fills the pipeline.

Which fire protection software records inspections and deficiencies?

Inspect Point is a fire inspection platform built for fire protection contractors. It records digital inspections, tracks deficiencies and builds reports for the inspection standard you work to.

  • Inspect Point: its plans are Silver, Gold and Platinum. Silver covers digital inspections, deficiency management and built-in NFPA and ULC compliant reports. Gold adds proposals built from deficiencies. Platinum adds work orders, API readiness and phone support. Prices are not published. Limit: plans start at three technicians, or one or two technicians running 400 or more inspections a year. The mobile app runs only on Apple devices.

The Gold feature is the one to weigh. A deficiency found on a sprinkler or alarm inspection is a repair sale waiting to happen. A tool that turns that finding into a proposal saves the evening you would spend retyping it. Ask for a demo using one of your own inspection reports, not a sample.

If you run fewer than the plan minimums, you may be better served by a general field service app plus your own report template. That is a real trade-off. You give up built-in compliance reports and keep a lower monthly bill.

Which fire protection software runs scheduling, quotes and invoices?

Housecall Pro and Joist cover the office side. Housecall Pro schedules and dispatches crews. Joist writes estimates and invoices.

  • Housecall Pro: online booking, scheduling, dispatch, estimates, invoicing, payments and review management. Basic is $59 a month billed annually, or $79 billed monthly, for one user. Essentials is $149 billed annually for five users, and Max is $299 billed annually for eight users. Limit: several add-ons are listed without prices, and card rates start at 2.59%, so confirm your total.
  • Joist: estimates, invoices and online payments in a light app. Joist Pro is $17 a month billed monthly, with unlimited documents. Limit: the lower Basics plan caps you at 5 documents a month, and payment processing fees apply on payments taken through Joist.

Pick Housecall Pro when several technicians share a calendar of recurring inspections. Pick Joist when one owner quotes repair work and invoices it. Either way, the inspection record stays in your fire inspection tool, and these apps handle the money and the schedule.

Recurring work needs a reminder habit. Set each commercial account to a due date and let the schedule remind you before the date, not after.

Which tool tracks the calls that bring in fire safety accounts?

CallRail is a call tracking tool that gives each marketing source its own number, so you can see which one produced a booked inspection. It does not record inspections or send proposals.

  • CallRail: its Lead Tracking plan is $50 a month and includes 5 local numbers, 250 local minutes and 25 texts. Plans bill monthly or yearly, with a 14-day free trial. Limit: usage above the included amounts is billed extra, and each added local number costs $3.

Fire safety companies often get calls from property managers, facility staff and building owners who found them in different places. Two numbers, one on the website and one on the Google listing, show whether search or your own site brings more requests. Add paid search later and give it a third number.

Which free tool puts a fire safety company on the map?

Google Business Profile is the free listing that shows your fire safety company in Google Maps and local search. Google states you can add or claim your business at no charge.

  • Google Business Profile: shows your name, service area, hours, photos and reviews when someone searches for fire protection services nearby. Limit: it only stands out if you keep services, photos and review replies current, and Google's paid ad products are separate.

List each service you sell as its own line, such as extinguisher service, alarm testing and sprinkler inspection. Searchers type the service, not the company type.

How much does fire protection software cost a year?

A lean fire protection stack costs $204 a year. A fuller stack with scheduling and call tracking costs $1,308 to $2,388 a year at published prices, before any Inspect Point quote.

ToolPublished priceYearly cost
Inspect PointNot publishedQuote in a demo
Housecall Pro Basic, billed annually$59 a month$708
Housecall Pro Basic, billed monthly$79 a month$948
Housecall Pro Essentials, billed annually$149 a month$1,788
Joist Pro, billed monthly$17 a month$204
CallRail Lead Tracking$50 a month$600
Google Business ProfileFree$0

Yearly cost is the published price multiplied out. Prices read from each vendor in November 2026.

Here is the arithmetic. The lean stack is Joist Pro at $17 a month plus a free listing, which is $204 a year. A mid stack is Housecall Pro Basic billed annually at $708 plus CallRail at $600, which is $1,308. A fuller stack is Housecall Pro Essentials at $1,788 plus CallRail at $600, which is $2,388.

Divide the yearly cost by your inspection count for the real price. As an example, $2,388 a year across 300 inspections is $7.96 per inspection. That is small next to one repair proposal, so judge each tool by the work it saves.

Add the Inspect Point quote on top of these figures. You cannot price it from the web. Ask for a written quote that lists technician count, plan tier and any setup fee.

How do you turn a deficiency into a repair sale?

Send the proposal within a day of the inspection, with the deficiency, the fix and one price. A finding that sits for a week loses urgency with the building owner.

  • Step 1: record the deficiency with a photo and the location inside the building.
  • Step 2: write the fix in plain words, such as "replace the failed alarm panel battery".
  • Step 3: price it from your own price list and send the proposal the same day.
  • Step 4: follow up once by phone, then set a reminder for the next inspection.

Gold-tier tools build the proposal from the finding. A general app can do it with a saved template. Either way, the habit of sending within a day is what earns the repair work.

What does fire protection software not do?

Fire protection software does not bring in new accounts. It records and organizes work you already have. A company with a thin pipeline needs lead sources before it needs a better inspection app.

It also does not replace your knowledge of the standards you work to. The tool formats the report, and your technician signs it. Confirm the format with your authority having jurisdiction before you send the first report.

What should you test in fire protection software before you buy?

Test the parts of the job that fire protection makes hard. Run these six checks inside each trial or demo.

  • Report format: does it produce the report your authority or customer expects, with your company details on it?
  • Deficiencies: can a finding become a quote line without retyping it?
  • Offline use: does the app work in a basement or a mechanical room with no signal?
  • Recurring dates: does each account carry a due date that triggers a reminder?
  • Devices: do your technicians use phones and tablets the tool supports?
  • Export: can you export inspection history if you leave?

A tool that fails two of these checks will cost time every week. Drop it, even if the price is lower. The device check matters, because one tool in this guide runs its mobile app on Apple devices only.

How do you choose fire protection software?

Choose fire protection software with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you pay.

Fit: does it record inspections the way your technicians work, and does it turn deficiencies into paid work?

Cost: add the plan price, extra users, payment fees and any technician minimum, then divide by your yearly inspection count.

Setup effort: can you load customers, sites and due dates in a weekend, or does it need onboarding?

A crew of 3 or more techniciansInspect Point demo and Housecall ProCallRail on the website and listingPlatinum features you will not use
A firm running paid searchAny inspection tool plus CallRailA managed website with a page per serviceAnything that duplicates your scheduler

Software does not create demand, so pair it with lead sources. Search ads from fire safety Google Ads reach buyers who need service now. Rankings from fire safety SEO bring steady local calls over time.

For the first impression, build a site with a page per service, such as extinguishers, alarms and sprinklers. Replies to reviews matter here too. See how to handle a negative review before you answer one.

What software does a fire protection company need?

A fire protection company needs inspection software, a way to quote repairs and a way to schedule recurring work. Inspect Point covers inspections and deficiencies, and Housecall Pro or Joist cover scheduling and billing. It also needs a free Google Business Profile so property managers can find it.

Published plans in this guide run from free for Google Business Profile to $299 a month for Housecall Pro Max, billed annually. Joist Pro lists $17 a month billed monthly. Inspect Point does not publish prices, so you request a quote in a demo.

Does Inspect Point publish its prices?

No. Inspect Point states that quotes are set by team size and trades, and you receive yours in a demo. Its plans start at three technicians, or one or two technicians running 400 or more inspections a year. Ask for a written quote with the tier and any setup fee.

Can a small fire safety company use general field service software?

Yes. Housecall Pro Basic lists $59 a month billed annually for one user, and Joist Pro lists $17 a month. You give up built-in compliance reports, so keep your own inspection template and confirm your customers accept the report format you send.

Do fire protection companies need call tracking?

Call tracking helps once you spend on more than one lead source. CallRail lists a Lead Tracking plan at $50 a month with 5 local numbers. Give each source its own number, then count booked inspections per number to see which marketing earns its cost.

Google states that you can add or claim your business at no charge. It still takes work: list each service you sell, upload photos of your work and reply to every review. Google's paid ad products are separate from the free listing.

Set up a free Google Business Profile and a quote app such as Joist Pro first. Then add a simple website with a page for each service. Request an Inspect Point demo once you have the technicians or inspection volume to meet its plan minimums.

###
What software does a fire protection company need?
A fire protection company needs inspection software, a way to quote repairs and a way to schedule recurring work. Inspect Point covers inspections and deficiencies, and Housecall Pro or Joist cover scheduling and billing. It also needs a free Google Business Profile so property managers can find it.
###
How much does fire protection software cost?
Published plans in this guide run from free for Google Business Profile to $299 a month for Housecall Pro Max, billed annually. Joist Pro lists $17 a month billed monthly. Inspect Point does not publish prices, so you request a quote in a demo.
###
Does Inspect Point publish its prices?
No. Inspect Point states that quotes are set by team size and trades, and you receive yours in a demo. Its plans start at three technicians, or one or two technicians running 400 or more inspections a year. Ask for a written quote with the tier and any setup fee.
###
Can a small fire safety company use general field service software?
Yes. Housecall Pro Basic lists $59 a month billed annually for one user, and Joist Pro lists $17 a month. You give up built-in compliance reports, so keep your own inspection template and confirm your customers accept the report format you send.
###
Do fire protection companies need call tracking?
Call tracking helps once you spend on more than one lead source. CallRail lists a Lead Tracking plan at $50 a month with 5 local numbers. Give each source its own number, then count booked inspections per number to see which marketing earns its cost.
###
Is Google Business Profile free for a fire safety company?
Google states that you can add or claim your business at no charge. It still takes work: list each service you sell, upload photos of your work and reply to every review. Google's paid ad products are separate from the free listing.
###
What should a new fire protection company buy first?
Set up a free Google Business Profile and a quote app such as Joist Pro first. Then add a simple website with a page for each service. Request an Inspect Point demo once you have the technicians or inspection volume to meet its plan minimums.
